title: Deductive proof and the binomial theorem
summary: Write short algebraic proofs from LHS to RHS, and expand (a + b)ⁿ with Pascal’s triangle and binomial coefficients.

keyterms.definition: An argument that reaches a conclusion by logical steps from known facts or definitions, valid for every case.
A statement true for every value of the variable, written with ≡, e.g. (x + 1)² ≡ x² + 2x + 1.
Proof method: start from one side of an identity and manipulate it until it becomes the other side.
An integer of the form 2n, where n ∈ ℤ.
An integer of the form 2n + 1, where n ∈ ℤ.
The expansion of (a + b)ⁿ as a sum of n + 1 terms ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ, r = 0, 1, …, n.
ⁿCᵣ = n! / (r!(n − r)!), the coefficient of aⁿ⁻ʳbʳ in (a + b)ⁿ.
A triangle of numbers in which each entry is the sum of the two above; row n gives the coefficients of (a + b)ⁿ.
The term ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ of a binomial expansion, used to find a specific coefficient without full expansion.

questions.prompt: Which expression represents any odd integer, where n ∈ ℤ?
questions.explanation: Every odd integer is one more than an even integer 2n.

questions.statement: Checking that a statement holds for n = 1, 2 and 3 proves it for all integers.
questions.explanation: Examples only support a conjecture; a proof must work for a general n.

options: Expand the left-hand side and simplify towards 12x
Assume 12x is true and work backwards
questions.explanation: Work from LHS to RHS: x² + 6x + 9 − (x² − 6x + 9) = 12x.

questions.text: The sum of consecutive integers n and n + 1 is 2n + 1, so it is always ___.
questions.explanation: 2n + 1 is the form of an odd integer for any integer n.

questions.prompt: (2m + 1)(2n + 1) simplifies to 2(2mn + m + n) + 1, where m, n ∈ ℤ. This proves that the product of two odd integers is…
questions.explanation: 2mn + m + n is an integer, so the product has the form 2k + 1.

questions.statement: The symbol ≡ means that the two sides are equal for every value of the variable.
questions.explanation: That is what distinguishes an identity from an equation, which holds only for particular values.

questions.text: n² + n = n(n + 1) is a product of consecutive integers, so it is always ___.
questions.explanation: One of any two consecutive integers is even, so their product is even.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Precise language and notation is part of the mark in proof questions.

questions.prompt: Order the proof that the sum of three consecutive integers is divisible by 3.
items: Let the integers be n, n + 1, n + 2
Since n + 1 is an integer, the sum is a multiple of 3
questions.explanation: A general representation, simplification, then a concluding sentence that refers back to the claim.
The difference of two squares. (a + b)² has a 2ab term that is often forgotten.
Each entry is the sum of the two above it in row 3 (1, 3, 3, 1): 3 + 3 = 6.

questions.prompt: Find the coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (1 + 2x)⁵.
questions.explanation: ⁵C₃ × 2³ = 10 × 8 = 80. Remember to cube the 2 as well as the x.

questions.prompt: How many terms are in the expansion of (a + b)¹⁰?
questions.explanation: (a + b)ⁿ has n + 1 terms, from r = 0 to r = n.

questions.statement: In the expansion of (x − 2)⁴, the constant term is 16.
questions.explanation: The constant term is ⁴C₄(−2)⁴ = 16; an even power makes it positive.

questions.prompt: Find the x² term in the expansion of (3 − x)⁴.
questions.explanation: ⁴C₂ × 3² × (−x)² = 6 × 9 × x² = 54x². The square makes the sign positive.
Choosing r items to take is the same as choosing n − r to leave, which is why Pascal’s triangle is symmetric.

questions.prompt: Match each expression to its expansion.
questions.explanation: Use Pascal’s triangle for the coefficients and include powers of every constant and sign.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to find the constant term of (x + 2/x)⁶.
items: Write the general term ⁶Cᵣ x⁶⁻ʳ (2/x)ʳ
Simplify the power of x to x⁶⁻²ʳ
questions.explanation: The general term lets you target one power of x without expanding everything.
